name: Crowell v. Benson
summary: The Supreme Court upheld an administrative workers' compensation scheme for maritime workers but drew a distinction between 'public rights' (which Congress may assign to agencies) and 'private rights' (which generally must be adjudicated in Article III courts).
significance: A landmark case on the limits of congressional power to assign adjudication to administrative agencies, establishing that certain 'private rights' require Article III adjudication — a distinction central to the dispute over H-2A enforcement.
